text.p: Talley Industries Inc said Tuesday Chief Executive Officer William Mallender resigned.
Mallender said in a statement it was in the best interest of Talley and its shareholders for him to resign following a recent shareholder vote where dissident shareholders sought his dismissal.
The company said in a statement last week Mallender lost his seat on the board of directors, which he had held since 1974, but that he would remain as chief executive.

The company said in a statement Tuesday it plans to offer the chief executive position to outside director Retired Admiral Paul Foster on an interim basis while it seeks out a successor. President and Chief Operating Officer Jack Crim will remain in his position.

The company also said it engaged J.P. Morgan Securities Inc to advise the board on strategic and financial alternatives available to the company. The board has set a special meeting later this month to consider the J.P. Morgan report and recommendations.

The board will also consider four proposals tabled by dissident shareholder group SCREAM (Shareholders Committee to remove Entrenched and Arrogant Management). Those proposals, whcih have been approved by shareholders, would eliminate staggered terms for directors, allow a 10 percent stockholder to call a special stockholders' meeting and approve the removal of anti-takeover provisions in the company's bylaws.
In the shareholder vote that cost Mallender his seat on the board SCREAM secured two seats on the company's board of directors.
